title: A non-blocking CompletableFuture chain

blocks.text: The page contrasts `Future.get()`, which blocks, with `CompletableFuture`, whose chain does not: `supplyAsync(...)` starts the work, `thenApply(...)` transforms its result when it arrives, and `exceptionally(...)` turns a failure into a value.
Write `Pipeline.run(executor, fetch, process, fallback)`, returning at once a `CompletableFuture<String>` that:

items: completes with `fallback` instead if `fetch` or `process` throws anything, an `Error` included, and otherwise waits for `fetch` however long it takes.

blocks.text: `run` itself must not wait for any of it.

rows: a fetch that waits for a signal
not done when `run` returns; `"DATA"` after the signal
`() -> Thread.currentThread().getName()` on an executor whose thread is `io-1`, `s -> s`

cases.says: The fetched value is passed through the processing step to the result.
run() returns an unfinished future at once instead of blocking until the fetch is done.
The fetch runs on the executor it was given, not on the common pool.
A failure in the fetch or the processing completes the future with the fallback instead of an exception.
A process that throws an Error, such as an AssertionError, also completes the future with the fallback.
A fetch that takes 5 s still completes the future with its processed value: there is no timeout of its own.

concepts: CompletableFuture chains supplyAsync, thenApply and exceptionally without blocking the caller.
